title: C8: surjectivity of the restriction map in degree two
statement:
Let $k$ be algebraically closed, let $C$ be a
smooth separated connected curve over $k$, let
$j:U\hookrightarrow C$ be an
open immersion, and let
$r$ be a prime. Then the constant sheaf $\mathbf F_r$ satisfies
$\mathcal C_8(C,\mathbf F_r)$ of
[def-weil-pbc-eight-curve-assertions]: the restriction map

$$
H^2(C_{\Et},\mathbf F_r)\longrightarrow
H^2(U_{\Et},\mathbf F_r)
$$

is surjective.

proof.text: Split according to whether the open immersion a:W→C is surjective. If it is, it is an isomorphism and therefore a universal homeomorphism. Topological invariance of etale cohomology gives bijectivity, hence surjectivity, for the underlying abelian constant coefficient sheaf.

Suppose a is not surjective. Smoothness makes C regular, and connectedness makes it irreducible. If C has dimension one, compactify C into a smooth proper connected curve Z using lem-sc-compactification. The image V of W in Z is not all of Z: otherwise injectivity of C→Z would make W→C surjective. By lem-sc-affine-open-proper V is affine; the isomorphism W≅V makes W affine. If C has dimension zero, irreducibility and the T0 property imply that C is a singleton (use the proved subsingleton_of_topologicalKrullDim_le_zero lemma); the open immersion embeds W into this singleton, so W is a subsingleton scheme and hence affine.

The open W is again a curve: it is quasi-compact because C is Noetherian, and its dimension is at most that of C. The constant coefficient sheaf Λ/rΛ is r-torsion, as is its inverse image on W. Apply lem-sc-affine-curve-h2-vanishing to this inverse image sheaf on the affine curve W. Its H² is a subsingleton, so every target class equals the image of zero. This constructs the required surjection without needing to identify the inverse image constant sheaf with a separately chosen constant sheaf on W.
